chapter: Jelly Roll's road trip, Benny Carter and Chick Webb
title: Early flute in jazz and why he dislikes the flute
summary: Wayman Carver was among the first Americans on flute in a jazz band after Cuban and Caribbean players; Procope says instruments go in and out of style and flute has no place in jazz.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Now, was anyone playing flute at that time, or was it -- was Wayman Carver the first?
Was that very unusual when he started playing with Chick?

No, not really. Not really, because there was another fellow named {Alberto} Socarras. Well, he was a Cuban, I believe, and he played with different bands, like Benny Carter's band and so and so, up at the Savoy, and he used to play the flute. And there were others, there was another band up there -- what was the name of this band? A band called the San Domingans. Yeah, they were from San Domingo, the band, and they were -- I wouldn't say it was a great band, but it was adequate for the Savoy and I think their leader's name was Napoleon, as I remember. You never heard of them, though?
Well, anyway, they had a flute, one or two flute players I think, because the musicians from the islands down there, Puerto Rico, Cuba, you know, a whole lot of them played flute.
But Wayman Carver, I believe, was one of the first Americans who played flute in a jazz band as such. Yeah.
Now it's very common for saxophone players to also play flute.
Oh, yes. See, instruments come in
style, like a few years back a bass saxophone came in style, and they played bass saxophone. Duke bought me a bass saxophone. I've still got it up there in the closet.

Yeah. Like I say, you know, it came in style and it had a vogue for a year or a couple of years, and then it went out and just like flutes. You can't get a job now in a lot of places. A lot of people ask me, "Do you play flute?" I say, "Hell, no." I say, "I don't even like a flute." I don't.
A flute is all right in its place, like in a symphony, but I don't think a flute has any place in jazz. There's nothing -- you can't even bend a note on a flute. Not to my mind.
